celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿ن﴾: one of the letters of the alphabet; Allah knows best what He means by it. ﴿وَالْقَلَمِ﴾ with which the created things were written in the Preserved Tablet, ﴿وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ﴾, i.e. the angels, of good and righteousness:

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿مَا أَنْتَ﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾, i.e. madness is negated from you because of your Lord's favouring you with prophethood and other things. This is a rebuttal of their saying that he is mad.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ لَكَ لَأَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ﴾ cut off.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَسَتُبْصِرُ وَيُبْصِرُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿بِأَيِّكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ﴾: a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الْمَعْقُولُ, i.e. الْفُتُونُ, in the sense of madness; i.e. is it in you or in them?

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾ to it; and أَعْلَمُ is in the sense of عَالِمٌ (knowing).

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿فَلَا تُطِعِ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَدُّوا﴾ they wished ﴿لَوْ﴾ — maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar) — ﴿تُدْهِنُ﴾ you would be soft with them ﴿فَيُدْهِنُونَ﴾ and they would be soft with you. It is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تُدْهِنُ; and if it is made the answer to the wish understood from وَدُّوا, هُمْ is implied before it, after the fāʾ.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَلَا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍ﴾ who swears much falsely, ﴿مَهِينٍ﴾ contemptible,

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿هَمَّازٍ﴾ a fault-finder, i.e. a backbiter, ﴿مَشَّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ﴾ going about with talk among people in order to sow discord among them,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ﴾ stingy with wealth against (others') rights, ﴿مُعْتَدٍ﴾ unjust, ﴿أَثِيمٍ﴾ sinful,

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿عُتُلٍّ﴾ coarse and harsh, ﴿بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ زَنِيمٍ﴾ a falsely attached member of Quraysh — he is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, whom his father claimed after eighteen years. Ibn ʿAbbās said: We do not know that Allah described anyone with the faults with which He described him, so He attached to him a shame that will never leave him. And the adverbial (ẓarf) before it is attached to زَنِيمٍ.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿أَنْ كَانَ ذَا مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾, i.e. لِأَنْ (because), and it is attached to what is indicated by:

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿إِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِ آيَاتُنَا﴾ the Quran, ﴿قَالَ﴾ they are ﴿أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾, i.e. he denied them because of Our favouring him with what is mentioned. And in a reading [أَأَنْ], with two hamzas with fatḥa. [Translator's note: the source has كَذَبَ بِهَا; the sense requires كَذَّبَ, "he denied", and it is translated so.]

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ﴾: We shall put a mark on his nose by which he will be reproached as long as he lives; and his nose was slashed by the sword on the day of Badr.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿إِنَّا بَلَوْنَاهُمْ﴾ We tested the people of Mecca with drought and hunger ﴿كَمَا بَلَوْنَا أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ the orchard, ﴿إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا﴾ that they would cut its fruit ﴿مُصْبِحِينَ﴾ at the time of morning, so that the poor would not notice them, and so they would not give them from it what their father used to give them in charity from it,

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ﴾ in their oath, by (saying) "if Allah the Exalted wills"; and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), i.e. and that was their way.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَائِفٌ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾: a fire that burned it by night, ﴿وَهُمْ نَائِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَالصَّرِيمِ﴾ like the intensely dark night, i.e. black.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿فَتَنَادَوْا مُصْبِحِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿أَنِ اغْدُوا عَلَى حَرْثِكُمْ﴾ your crop — an explication (tafsīr) of تَنَادَوْا, or أَنْ is maṣdariyya, i.e. بِأَنْ — ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَارِمِينَ﴾ intending to cut; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is indicated by what precedes it.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿فَانْطَلَقُوا وَهُمْ يَتَخَافَتُونَ﴾ whispering to one another:

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿أَنْ لَا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِسْكِينٌ﴾: an explication (tafsīr) of what precedes it, or أَنْ is maṣdariyya, i.e. بِأَنْ.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَغَدَوْا عَلَى حَرْدٍ﴾ withholding from the poor, ﴿قَادِرِينَ﴾ upon it, in their opinion.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهَا﴾ black and burnt, ﴿قَالُوا إِنَّا لَضَالُّونَ عَنْهَا﴾, i.e. this is not it. Then they said, when they recognised it:

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ﴾ of its fruit, for our withholding it from the poor.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿قَالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ﴾ the best of them: ﴿أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكُمْ لَوْلَا﴾ why do you not ﴿تُسَبِّحُونَ﴾ Allah, repenting?

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿قَالُوا سُبْحَانَ رَبِّنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ by withholding from the poor their right.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ يَتَلَاوَمُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا﴾ — for alerting (tanbīh) — ﴿وَيْلَنَا﴾ our ruin! ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا طَاغِينَ﴾

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿عَسَى رَبُّنَا أَنْ يُبَدِّلَنَا﴾, with tashdīd and without it [يُبْدِلَنَا], ﴿خَيْرًا مِنْهَا إِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا رَاغِبُونَ﴾, that He accept our repentance and give us back better than our orchard. It is narrated that they were given better than it in exchange.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾, i.e. like the punishment for these, is ﴿الْعَذَابُ﴾ for whoever opposes Our command among the disbelievers of Mecca and others; ﴿وَلَعَذَابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ its punishment, they would not have opposed Our command. And there was revealed, when they said, "If we are resurrected, we will be given better than you":

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿أَفَنَجْعَلُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ كَالْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾, i.e. following them in what is given?

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿مَا لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ﴾ this corrupt judgement?

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾, i.e. بَلْ أَ (rather, is it that), ﴿لَكُمْ كِتَابٌ﴾ revealed ﴿فِيهِ تَدْرُسُونَ﴾, i.e. you read,

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿إِنَّ لَكُمْ فِيهِ لَمَا تَخَيَّرُونَ﴾ you choose?

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمَانٌ﴾ covenants ﴿عَلَيْنَا بَالِغَةٌ﴾ binding ﴿إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَمَةِ﴾ — attached in meaning to عَلَيْنَا; and in this speech there is the meaning of an oath, i.e. "We swore to you" — and its apodosis is: ﴿إِنَّ لَكُمْ لَمَا تَحْكُمُونَ﴾ for yourselves?

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿سَلْهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ بِذَلِكَ﴾ — the judgement they pass for themselves, that they will be given in the Hereafter better than the believers — ﴿زَعِيمٌ﴾ a guarantor for them?

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ﴾, i.e. with them, ﴿شُرَكَاءُ﴾ agreeing with them in this saying, guaranteeing it for them? If it is so, ﴿فَلْيَأْتُوا بِشُرَكَائِهِمْ﴾ who guarantee it for them, ﴿إِنْ كَانُوا صَادِقِينَ﴾. Mention:

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ سَاقٍ﴾: it is an expression for the severity of the matter on the Day of Resurrection, for the reckoning and recompense; it is said "the war has bared its shank" (kashafat al-ḥarbu ʿan sāq) when the matter in it becomes severe. ﴿وَيُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ﴾ as a test of their أَيْمَان [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source, "oaths"; it is likely meant as إِيمَان, "faith".], ﴿فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾: their backs become a single plate,

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿خَاشِعَةً﴾ — a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of يُدْعَوْنَ, i.e. humbled — ﴿أَبْصَارُهُمْ﴾: they do not raise them; ﴿تَرْهَقُهُمْ﴾ covers them ﴿ذِلَّةٌ وَقَدْ كَانُوا يُدْعَوْنَ﴾ in this world ﴿إِلَى السُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سَالِمُونَ﴾, yet they did not do it, in that they did not pray.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿فَذَرْنِي﴾ leave Me ﴿وَمَنْ يُكَذِّبُ بِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ﴾ the Quran; ﴿سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ﴾ We shall take them little by little ﴿مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ﴾ I give them respite; ﴿إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ﴾ severe, unbearable.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ rather, do ﴿تَسْأَلُهُمْ﴾ for conveying the message ﴿أَجْرًا فَهُمْ مِنْ مَغْرَمٍ﴾ of what they give you ﴿مُثْقَلُونَ﴾, and so they do not believe because of that?

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿أَمْ عِنْدَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ﴾, i.e. the Preserved Tablet in which is the unseen, ﴿فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ﴾ from it what they say?

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ﴾ concerning them, with what He wills, ﴿وَلَا تَكُنْ كَصَاحِبِ الْحُوتِ﴾ in vexation and haste — he is Jonah (Yūnus), upon him be peace — ﴿إِذْ نَادَى﴾ called upon his Lord ﴿وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ﴾ filled with grief, in the belly of the fish.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿لَوْلَا أَنْ تَدَارَكَهُ﴾ reached him ﴿نِعْمَةٌ﴾ mercy ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ﴾ from the belly of the fish ﴿بِالْعَرَاءِ﴾ on the open land ﴿وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ﴾; but he was shown mercy, so he was cast out not blameworthy.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿فَاجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ﴾ with prophethood ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ the prophets.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿وَإِنْ يَكَادُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾, with ḍamma on the yāʾ and with fatḥa, ﴿بِأَبْصَارِهِمْ﴾, i.e. they look at you with an intense look that almost fells you and makes you fall from your place, ﴿لَمَّا سَمِعُوا الذِّكْرَ﴾ the Quran, ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ out of envy: ﴿إِنَّهُ لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾ because of the Quran he has brought.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿وَمَا هُوَ﴾, i.e. the Quran, ﴿إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ﴾ an admonition ﴿لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ jinn and humans; no madness arises because of it.
